title: The potential of harmaline on triple negative breast cancer: harmaline-DNA interaction related apoptosis, anti-metastasis, and in silico analysis.
authors: Subramanian, Srividya; Guguloth, Sai Krishna; Pajaniradje, Sankar; Bhat, Suhail Ahmad; Chandramohan, Sathyapriya; Vishnumaya, A P; Suresh Nair, Anjali; Archana, V K; Subramanian, Suci; Rajagopalan, Rukkumani
one_liner_zh: 研究harmaline与DNA的混合结合模式及抗癌机制，虽涉及DNA互作和分子对接，但对象为小分子-核酸而非蛋白质-DNA，且无AI/物理模拟方法创新，与TF-DNA课题关联较弱。
abstract: Breast cancer, particularly triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), remains a therapeutic challenge owing to limited targeted treatment options and high metastatic potential. This study aimed to investigate the in vitro and in silico anticancer effects of harmaline, a naturally occurring beta-carboline alkaloid, against the MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cell line, focusing on its cytotoxic, apoptotic, DNA-binding, and protein interaction potential. Cytotoxicity assessment by MTT assay revealed a significant reduction in cell viability with an IC(50) value of 99.53 microM, further confirmed by LDH release indicating membrane damage. Apoptosis induction was evidenced through Annexin V/PI staining, DNA fragmentation, nuclear condensation, and mitochondrial depolarization. Morphological alterations and wound healing assays demonstrated harmaline's ability to inhibit migration, indicating its anti-migratory activity. Flow cytometry revealed G2/M phase cell cycle arrest, implicating interference with DNA replication and repair processes. Biophysical studies, including ultraviolet-visible (UV-Vis), fluorescence, circular dichroism, FTIR, and KI quenching analyses demonstrated that harmaline interacts with DNA through a mixed binding mode involving both intercalative and groove-associated interactions, leading to conformational alterations in the DNA helix. Complementary molecular docking studies showed harmaline interacting with key cancer-associated proteins with moderate affinity, supporting a multi-target therapeutic mechanism. These results position harmaline as a promising candidate for further preclinical development and structure-based optimization in breast cancer therapy.
abstract_zh: 乳腺癌，尤其是三阴性乳腺癌（TNBC），由于靶向治疗选择有限且转移潜力高，仍是治疗上的挑战。本研究旨在探讨天然存在的β-咔啉生物碱哈尔明碱（harmaline）对MDA-MB-231乳腺癌细胞系的体外及计算机模拟抗癌作用，重点关注其细胞毒性、凋亡诱导、DNA结合及蛋白质相互作用潜力。通过MTT法评估细胞毒性，结果显示细胞活力显著降低，IC(50)值为99.53微摩尔，并通过LDH释放进一步确认，表明膜损伤。凋亡诱导通过Annexin V/PI染色、DNA片段化、核浓缩及线粒体去极化得到证实。形态学改变和伤口愈合实验表明，哈尔明碱具有抑制迁移的能力，显示其抗迁移活性。流式细胞术揭示G2/M期细胞周期阻滞，提示其干扰DNA复制和修复过程。生物物理研究，包括紫外-可见（UV-Vis）、荧光、圆二色、FTIR及KI淬灭分析，表明哈尔明碱通过涉及嵌入和沟槽相关相互作用的混合结合模式与DNA相互作用，导致DNA螺旋构象改变。补充的分子对接研究表明，哈尔明碱以中等亲和力与关键癌症相关蛋白相互作用，支持多靶点治疗机制。这些结果将哈尔明碱定位为乳腺癌治疗中进一步临床前开发和基于结构的优化的有前景候选物。
